basis: Hereditary amyloid neuropathy; cardiac amyloid involvement commonly exceeds 30%; sensorineural hearing loss in 2/4. GI symptoms may reflect autonomic neuropathy.
Brain malformations, developmental delay, cardiac and digital defects define syndrome; hearing loss 2/3. Ocular anomalies and sparse hair omitted at four-axis cap.
Biliary tree disease; intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts and gallbladder fall within hepatic.
Congenital skin creases, intellectual disability and microphthalmia in 4/4; cleft palate in 3/4 supports gastrointestinal involvement.
Progressive chorioretinal degeneration with impaired vision; corneal and retinal abnormalities remain within the ocular axis.
Inflammation of the esophageal wall; the umbrella includes reflux, infectious and immune-mediated subtypes without a shared immune mechanism.
Brain commissural malformations and developmental impairment define the neurologic disorder; progressive scoliosis is defining. Gaze palsy is supranuclear.
Epilepsy, intellectual deterioration and defective dental enamel define syndrome; hypohidrosis represents sweat-gland dysfunction in 30–79%.
Inherited bile-metabolism disorder with cholestasis/cirrhosis; glomerulosclerosis 2/2 and developmental delay 3/3. Splenomegaly is secondary to liver disease.
Defining ectodermal defects affect hair, skin, sweat glands and teeth; endocrine abnormalities are occasional, not intrinsic defining features.
Acute inflammation of the vermiform appendix; an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism is not universal.
Androgenetic miniaturization of scalp hair follicles; androgen sensitivity does not establish an endocrine gland disorder.
Ocular anomalies, shortened skeletal elements and hair/pigment abnormalities define syndrome; congenital anodontia is characteristic in the reported siblings.
Defined as a CAMK2A-related neurodevelopmental disorder; no additional organ damage is established across its subtypes.
Defined as a productive HPV infection of vulvar epithelium; reproductive location has no organ axis, but the infection mechanism qualifies.
Sarcomatoid variant of basal cell carcinoma arising in skin; spindle-cell morphology does not establish musculoskeletal origin.
Chronic immune-mediated skin disease; oral mucosal involvement occurs in roughly half. Associated hepatitis C is a separate infection.
Senior-Loken syndrome combines nephronophthisis and retinal degeneration; mild intellectual disability in 6/19 (~32%) just meets the involvement threshold.
Central saccade-initiation disorder; ataxia 80–99% and cerebellar abnormalities 30–79% support neurologic localization. Intrinsic eye injury is not established.
Tumor arises in uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Adrenal steroid synthesis deficiency causes cortisol and aldosterone deficiency; renal salt loss reflects hormonal deficiency rather than intrinsic kidney damage.
Immature teratoma arises in the central nervous system; tumor origin determines the organ axis.
Opacity of the crystalline lens directly impairs vision; causes vary across this umbrella concept.
Fibronectin deposition damages renal glomeruli; hypertension and acidosis are secondary manifestations without evidence of additional intrinsic organ disease.
Inherited immunodeficiency; retinal, gastrointestinal and skin manifestations lack frequencies establishing common direct involvement; associated infections are separate diseases.
